audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere connects Fury of the Sands to Feast's health stacking. The guide treats Cho'Gath growing fat as purely bad news.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands carries the percentHealth flag — Riot's derived note on it is literally 'punishes HP stacking — armour alone is not the answer' — and Feast's whole identity is 'If the target is killed, Cho'Gath grows, gaining maximum Health.' The two interact directly and in Nasus's favour: every Feast stack Cho'Gath banks makes Nasus's ultimate hit him harder. This inverts the emotional read of the matchup, which currently tells a Nasus that a stacked Cho'Gath is a scaling problem when he is in fact the single best target in the game for Nasus's ult. It is the best thing available to say here and it is absent.

audit.whatIsWrong: The item block is Trinity Force into Frozen Heart with Plated Steelcaps — three resistance items — in the one matchup where _missing-interactions.json explicitly says resistances are the wrong answer.
audit.why: The flagged interaction is 'Cho'Gath bypasses stacking resistances (Feast (R)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here.' Feast is true damage, so armour does nothing against the ability that actually kills Nasus. What keeps him alive is raw health, because Feast is a threshold execute and health is what moves the threshold out of reach. The current build advice is the intuitive one and the wrong one.
audit.corrected: Added the buy-health-for-the-threshold note to the item line, trimming the redundant Sheen sentence that the Trinity Force entry already implies.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns lists Rupture twice: '- Cho'Gath Rupture (Knockup): matchup-defining — Telegraphed. Dodge it. - Cho'Gath Rupture: Delayed ground spike that knocks up and slows'. The second entry is the same ability described again.
audit.why: Same duplicate-entry defect as the Aurora block. It wastes the only slot in the section that could name Feral Scream, which is the ability that actually beats Nasus — a silence stops Siphoning Strike, and Siphoning Strike is his entire damage output and his entire scaling mechanism.
audit.corrected: Replaced the duplicate with Feral Scream and its real numbers, 11s at rank 1 and 300 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feast is described as 'a flat percent-HP true-damage execute' in whys[4] and as 'true-damage percent-HP R that ignores your lifesteal' in wants.foe[2].
audit.why: Three problems in two strings. 'Flat' and 'percent-HP' are contradictory. Riot's text says only 'a high amount of true damage' with no percent-health damage component — the percentHealth flag on Feast refers to the maximum-health growth on kill, not to the damage. And true damage does not 'ignore your lifesteal'; lifesteal is Nasus healing from his own damage and is unaffected by the type of damage he receives. What Feast actually ignores is armour and magic resist.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both to say Feast is a large true-damage execute that ignores resistances.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers for Cho'Gath appear anywhere, and Feral Scream's range is never given.
audit.why: Two numbers carry this matchup. Rupture is a flat 6s at every rank — it never gets shorter as he levels it, so there is no 'wait for it to come off cooldown' window worth planning around, which is the opposite of how most matchups work. Feral Scream is 11s at rank 1 and only 300 range, which is shorter than most players assume and is the actual line a Nasus must respect: outside 300 units the silence cannot land and Siphoning Strike always goes off.
audit.corrected: Added both figures to breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, phases[2].why, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[1].d and content.mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json Q cooldown '6', W cooldown 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 and range 300

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1] titled 'Get silenced mid-Q' carries the same 'Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown' string as every other matchup in this slice; dosFull[2] titled 'Dodge his Q and W' is described as 'Cho'Gath wastes Rupture (Knockup) — commit the full pattern immediately'.
audit.why: Eight of eight matchups in this slice carry the dontsFull[1].d defect and seven of eight carry a mismatched dosFull[2].d. Both are template-level bugs in whatever generated champ-data/nasus.full.js and should be fixed at the generator rather than 71 times by hand.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both to match their titles with real cooldown and range numbers.

audit.why: 51.6% over 407 games matches MC_WR_TABLES, and the chart [Skill, Skill, Cho'Gath x4, Nasus] is consistent with a near-even lane that Nasus scales out of. No contradiction flagged.

The trading advice is the most accurate in this slice — it correctly identifies Rupture into Feral Scream as the only real all-in window, correctly says a silence means no Wither and no Spirit Fire, and correctly tells the player to use Wither defensively on his step-up rather than as an engage tool. I found nothing to correct here and left it alone apart from substituting real ability names.

edits.before: This is his window, not mine. With Q-W up he can knock me up, silence me, and win the short trade before I have the stacks or Sheen to answer, and at 6 his Feast is a flat execute — if I'm chunked, walking into R range is just dying. Use Wither defensively here: the instant he steps for a Q, slow him so the knockup whiffs and the silence never lands. Don't all-in him in this stretch; farm, soak, and wait for items.
edits.after: This is his window, not mine. With Rupture and Feral Scream up he can knock me up, silence me, and win the short trade before I have the stacks or Sheen to answer, and at 6 Feast is true damage — if I'm chunked, stepping inside its 175 range is just dying. Use Wither defensively here: the instant he steps for a Rupture, slow him so the knockup whiffs and the silence never lands. Don't all-in him; farm and wait for items.

edits.before: Now it flips to me. Once I have real Q stacks plus Sheen and Fury of the Sands, Wither turns his Q-W combo off entirely — he can't land the knockup or close the gap — and my empowered Q chunks through his fat HP bar faster than his R execute can save him. His true-damage Feast still hurts, so I want the fight long: my lifesteal and ult outlast a single R while my Q keeps hitting. Lock him with Wither, E for the armor shred, and grind him down.
edits.after: Now it flips to me. Once I have real Q stacks plus Sheen and Fury of the Sands, Wither turns his Rupture-into-Feral-Scream combo off entirely, and my empowered Q chunks through his fat HP bar. Better still, every Feast stack he banked feeds my ult — Fury of the Sands scales its damage off his max health, so the fatter he grew the harder it lands. Feast's true damage still ignores my armour, so I want the fight long and my lifesteal outlasts one R.

notes: The suspectName flag on content.mid ('With Q-' looksLike 'wither', distance 3) is a false positive — the source text is 'With Q-W up', the ordinary English word 'With' followed by the ability letters. No change made on that basis. Best find here is a positive one rather than a correction: Fury of the Sands carries the percentHealth flag and Feast permanently grants maximum health, so Cho'Gath's own scaling mechanic makes him progressively more vulnerable to Nasus's ultimate. Worth checking whether other percent-health owners in the roster (and other HP-stacking enemies such as Sion) are missing the same interaction — it is the kind of thing a flag-crossing pass over kitFlags would surface automatically for every pairing at once. NOT ASSERTED: whether Feral Scream's silence, if it lands after Siphoning Strike has been cast but before the empowered auto-attack connects, cancels the empowered attack or leaves it armed. This is the single most decisive unknown in the matchup for a Nasus, since it determines whether Q is safe to pre-cast while he is in range. needsResearch.animationCancels is null for both champions and Riot's text does not cover it, so I left the topic alone entirely rather than guess. It deserves a wiki pass or an in-client test. No WKM_LINES problems seen for this pairing.
